compensating.why: hop 1 decodes escaped slashes in the expression before the segments are linked
hop 3 places the segment on the expression with escaped slashes decoded
hop 4 hands the decoder the expression with escaped slashes decoded

ownership_reason: Only the segment decoder reads the characters of a segment; the facade, the pass-throughs, the placement step and the fold hand down the raw expression and offsets computed on it. Once the decoder has kept an escaped slash as the two characters '~1' the name is ambiguous ('~1' and '~01' both come out as '~1'), so no caller can recover it: a post-hoc replace("~1", "/") turns '~01', which stands for '~1', into '/' (the double decoding RFC 6901 section 4 warns against; JsonPointer._appendEscape decodes '~01' as '~1'), contradicting the documented decode. No caller can pre-filter: decoding '~1' in the expression before the fold splits the segment and changes every suffix string (toString), and decoding it below the fold shifts the offsets. The convention is pinned outside the gold by JsonPointer._appendEscape ('1' -> '/') and _parseQuotedTail, the class javadoc's reference to the JSON Pointer specification, and the trigger's own expectations ('w~1out' -> 'w/out', 'a~1b' -> 'a/b'); the other TestJsonPointer tests pin the boundaries, suffix strings and plain names that the non-gold hops produce.
